problems.quote: Under the Indian Contract Act, 1872 (specifically Section 10 and subsequent sections on remedies)
problems.problem: Section 10 defines valid contracts, not remedies; specific performance is governed by the Specific Relief Act, 1963, not the Contract Act.
problems.correction: Under the Indian Contract Act, 1872 (Sections 73–75 for damages) and the Specific Relief Act, 1963 for specific performance
problems.verifierReason: Section 10 defines valid contracts; remedies are in Sections 73-75 and Specific Relief Act.

problems.quote: Specific Performance of Contracts v. Union of India
problems.problem: No such Supreme Court case exists; the landmark case on specific performance is K. K. Verma v. Union of India (1954) or Union of India v. Raman Iron Foundry (1974).
problems.correction: K. K. Verma v. Union of India
problems.verifierReason: No such case exists; K.K. Verma is a landmark case on specific performance.

problems.quote: State of Bombay v. R.M.D. Chamarbaugwala
problems.problem: This case is not about frustration; the leading case on frustration under Section 56 is Satyabrata Ghose v. Mugneeram Bangur & Co. (1954).
problems.correction: Satyabrata Ghose v. Mugneeram Bangur & Co.
problems.verifierReason: Case is not on frustration; Satyabrata Ghose is the leading case on Section 56.

problems.quote: Section 91 states that a contract or the terms thereof, or any material particular thereof, relating to the soundness of the mind or sanity of a person, cannot be proved by oral evidence if the docume
problems.problem: Section 91 of the Evidence Act deals with documentary evidence of contracts and does not mention soundness of mind; that concept appears in other sections.
problems.correction: Section 91 states that when the terms of a contract have been reduced to a document, no evidence shall be given except the document itself or secondary evidence.
problems.verifierReason: Section 91 deals with documentary evidence, not soundness of mind; correction accurately states its content.

problems.quote: Section 49 of Transfer of Property Act
problems.problem: Section 49 of the Transfer of Property Act concerns transferee's rights under a policy, not writing requirements for immovable property contracts.
problems.correction: Section 54 of the Transfer of Property Act and Section 17 of the Registration Act
problems.verifierReason: Section 49 concerns insurance policy rights; writing requirements for immovable property are in Section 54 TPA and Section 17 Registration Act.

problems.quote: Section 126 of Contract Act
problems.problem: Section 126 defines a guarantee but does not require it to be in writing; Indian law does not mandate written guarantees.
problems.correction: Section 126 of the Contract Act defines guarantee but does not impose a writing requirement
problems.verifierReason: Section 126 defines guarantee without writing requirement; correction correctly states this.

problems.quote: with at least one‑third of the board comprising independent directors where the chairperson is executive; if the chairperson is non‑executive, at least half the board must be independent
problems.problem: The independent director requirement is reversed: if chairperson is executive, at least half the board must be independent; if chairperson is non‑executive, at least one‑third must be independent.
problems.correction: with at least half of the board comprising independent directors where the chairperson is executive; if the chairperson is non‑executive, at least one‑third of the board must be independent
problems.verifierReason: Original reverses SEBI LODR Reg 17(1) rule; correction states correct thresholds.

problems.quote: Recent amendments (SEBI LODR (Amendment) Regulations, 2023) have introduced a “board skill matrix” disclosure
problems.problem: The board skill matrix disclosure was introduced by SEBI LODR (Amendment) Regulations, 2021, not 2023.
problems.correction: Recent amendments (SEBI LODR (Amendment) Regulations, 2021) introduced a “board skill matrix” disclosure
problems.verifierReason: Board skill matrix introduced by 2021 amendment, not 2023; correction fixes year.

problems.quote: The amendments also tighten the tenure of independent directors — a person cannot serve as an independent director for more than two consecutive terms of five years each, and a cooling‑off period of t
problems.problem: The tenure limits (two five‑year terms, three‑year cooling‑off) are from the Companies Act, 2013, not introduced or tightened by the 2023 LODR amendments.
problems.correction: The Companies Act, 2013 limits independent directors to two consecutive five‑year terms with a three‑year cooling‑off period.
problems.verifierReason: Tenure limits are from Companies Act 2013, not LODR amendments; correction correctly attributes.

problems.quote: expected rate of return on plan assets (used only for determining the net interest component)
problems.problem: Under Ind AS 19, the expected rate of return on plan assets is not an actuarial assumption; the discount rate is used to calculate net interest on both the obligation and plan assets.
problems.correction: discount rate used for plan assets' net interest component
problems.verifierReason: Ind AS 19 (revised 2015) replaced expected return on plan assets with interest income calculated using the discount rate; the quote reflects the superseded standard.

problems.quote: on the direction of the recipient, the place of supply is the principal place of business of that person (Section 10(1)(b))
problems.problem: Section 10(1)(b) of the IGST Act states the place of supply is the principal place of business of the person when goods are delivered on the direction of a third person, not the recipient.
problems.correction: on the direction of a third person, the place of supply is the principal place of business of that person (Section 10(1)(b))
problems.verifierReason: Original misstates recipient for third person; correction matches IGST Act Sec 10(1)(b).

problems.quote: The 2021 amendment (Companies (Amendment) Act, 2021) introduced the concept of “impact assessment”
problems.problem: Impact assessment for CSR was introduced by the Companies (CSR Policy) Amendment Rules, 2021, not the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2021.
problems.correction: The 2021 amendment (Companies (CSR Policy) Amendment Rules, 2021) introduced the concept of “impact assessment”
problems.verifierReason: Original cites wrong Act; impact assessment introduced by CSR Policy Amendment Rules 2021.

problems.quote: limited to original impairment on depreciable assets (₹10 crore)
problems.problem: Ind AS 36 limits reversal to the carrying amount that would have been determined (net of depreciation) had no impairment loss been recognised, not simply the original impairment amount.
problems.correction: limited to the carrying amount net of depreciation had no impairment been recognised
problems.verifierReason: Ind AS 36 reversal cap is carrying amount net of depreciation had no impairment been recognised, not original impairment amount.

problems.quote: its reported revenue, profit or loss, or assets are 10 % or more of the combined revenue, profit or loss, or assets of all operating segments
problems.problem: The profit/loss threshold is not 10% of combined profit or loss; it is 10% of the greater (in absolute amount) of combined profits of profitable segments and combined losses of loss-making segments.
problems.correction: its revenue or assets ≥10% of combined totals, or |profit/loss| ≥10% of greater of combined profits/losses
problems.verifierReason: Segment profit/loss threshold uses greater of combined profits/losses in absolute terms, not net combined profit/loss.

problems.quote: autobiographical prose work Meri Kavita Mere Geet
problems.problem: Meri Kavita Mere Geet is a poetry collection, not an autobiographical prose work.
problems.correction: poetry collection Meri Kavita Mere Geet
problems.verifierReason: Meri Kavita Mere Geet is a poetry collection by Ramdhari Singh Dinkar, not autobiographical prose.

problems.quote: (P_i - MC_i) / P_i = λ, where λ is a constant across all products
problems.problem: The Ramsey-Boiteux pricing rule states that the markup fraction (P_i - MC_i)/P_i should be inversely proportional to the price elasticity of demand, not constant across products.
problems.correction: (P_i - MC_i) / P_i = λ / |ε_i|, where λ is a constant and ε_i is the price elasticity of demand for product i
problems.verifierReason: Original misstates Ramsey rule; correction gives correct inverse elasticity formula.

problems.quote: Do not assume perfect price discrimination leads to zero consumer surplus without specifying if it is first, second, or third-degree
problems.problem: Perfect price discrimination is first-degree price discrimination by definition; it always leads to zero consumer surplus. The warning incorrectly implies "perfect price discrimination" could be second or third degree.
problems.correction: Do not assume price discrimination leads to zero consumer surplus without specifying if it is first, second, or third-degree
problems.verifierReason: Perfect price discrimination is first-degree; correction removes misleading 'perfect'.

problems.problem: The steady-state capital intensity formula for the Diamond OLG model with Cobb-Douglas production and log utility is incorrect; the correct formula includes (1-α) and (1+β) in the numerator.
problems.verifierReason: Original formula misses (1-α) and (1+β); correction matches standard Diamond OLG derivation.

problems.quote: increased the states’ share to 41 %
problems.problem: The 15th Finance Commission (2020‑25) reduced the states' share of central taxes from 42% (14th FC) to 41%, not increased it.
problems.correction: set the states’ share at 41 %
problems.verifierReason: 15th FC reduced share from 42% to 41%; 'increased' is wrong, 'set at' is accurate.

problems.quote: The Fourth Plan (1969‑74) introduced the “growth with social justice” slogan
problems.problem: The slogan "growth with social justice" was associated with the Sixth Plan (1980‑85), not the Fourth Plan.
problems.correction: The Sixth Plan (1980‑85) introduced the “growth with social justice” slogan
problems.verifierReason: Fourth Plan slogan was 'growth with stability'; Sixth Plan introduced 'growth with social justice'. Correction correct.

problems.quote: RBI’s reserve management policy targets a comfortable import cover (currently above 12 months)
problems.problem: As of 2024, India's import cover is around 11 months, not above 12 months.
problems.correction: RBI’s reserve management policy targets a comfortable import cover (currently around 11 months)
problems.verifierReason: As of Mar 2024, import cover ~11.4 months, not >12. Correction 'around 11 months' is accurate.

problems.quote: rationalised the rate structure from 28 slabs to four main slabs
problems.problem: GST never had 28 slabs; it had four main slabs (5%, 12%, 18%, 28%) plus a few special rates.
problems.correction: rationalised the rate structure to four main slabs
problems.verifierReason: GST never had 28 slabs; launched with four main slabs. Correction removes false 'from 28 slabs'.

problems.quote: commitment savings accounts with default deposits raise formal savings by 20–30 % (Ashraf, Karlan, Yin 2006)
problems.problem: The cited study (Ashraf, Karlan, Yin 2006) tested a commitment savings product (not default deposits) and found an 81% increase in savings balances, not 20–30%.
problems.correction: commitment savings accounts raise formal savings by 81 % (Ashraf, Karlan, Yin 2006)
problems.verifierReason: Original misstates product (default deposits) and effect size (20-30%). Study tested commitment savings, found 81% increase. Correction accurate.

problems.quote: Hybrid Annuity Model” (HAM) and “Viability Gap Funding” (VGF) are used for metro, bus rapid transit and water supply projects.
problems.problem: HAM is a PPP model designed for highway projects (NHAI), not for metro, BRT, or water supply; VGF is used for those sectors.
problems.correction: Viability Gap Funding (VGF) is used for metro, bus rapid transit and water supply projects; the Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM) is primarily used for highway projects.
problems.verifierReason: HAM is NHAI's highway PPP model; VGF covers metro/BRT/water. Correction accurately separates them.

problems.quote: managed by the National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID)
problems.problem: The Urban Infrastructure Development Fund (UIDF) announced in the 2023‑24 budget is managed by the National Housing Bank (NHB), not NaBFID.
problems.correction: managed by the National Housing Bank (NHB)
problems.verifierReason: UIDF (2023-24 Budget) is managed by NHB, not NaBFID. Correction is factually correct.

problems.quote: The “National Urban Policy Framework” (2021) recommends a uniform LVC legislation
problems.problem: The National Urban Policy Framework was released in 2018, not 2021.
problems.correction: The “National Urban Policy Framework” (2018) recommends a uniform LVC legislation
problems.verifierReason: National Urban Policy Framework released in 2018, not 2021. Correction fixes the year accurately.
